section: Environmental Studies · Ch43 — Electricity — Deep Practice
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: Household electrical wiring uses parallel circuits rather than series circuits mainly because in a parallel circuit:

options.option_text: Each appliance gets the same full voltage and can operate independently, even if one fails
All appliances must always be switched on together
Only one appliance can be used at any given time
The voltage across each appliance is much less than the source voltage

explanation: Parallel wiring lets each appliance receive full source voltage and operate independently.

section: Environmental Studies · Ch43 — Electricity — Deep Practice
subject: Environmental Studies
stem: An electric fuse in household wiring is designed to:

options.option_text: Melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, preventing fire/damage
Increase the current flowing to appliances
Permanently connect all appliances regardless of current
Convert AC current to DC current

explanation: A fuse contains a wire that melts and breaks the circuit if current exceeds a safe threshold, protecting wiring from fire.
